title: Allu Arjun Flies to a Mirror, Not a Set. The AA23 Look Test Is the First Real Move in Bollywood-Tollywood's Most Dangerous Team-Up.
excerpt: Lokesh Kanagaraj lands in Mumbai on June 25 to lock the face of his Telugu debut. Pushpa's swagger, the LCU's darkness, and Anirudh on the console — the diaspora hasn't been this hungry for a first look in years.
body:
There is no set yet. No title that anyone will confirm on the record. No leaked frame, no teaser timed to midnight. And yet the single most anticipated piece of news in Indian cinema this week is a man sitting in front of a mirror in a Mumbai studio while a director decides how he should look.

That man is **Allu Arjun**, fresh off the planet-sized success of the *Pushpa* franchise, and the director circling him is **Lokesh Kanagaraj** — the architect of the LCU, the dark, interlocking action universe of *Kaithi*, *Vikram* and *Leo* that turned Tamil cinema into a high-stakes chess game. On June 25, Lokesh and his team fly to Mumbai to conduct the official look test for the project everyone is calling **AA23**, and the industry is treating it like a coronation.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=E8vqNHyOFWQ</youtube>


> "It's a proper pan-Indian film — not because of the stars, the central character, or the setting, but because the story has a very international appeal." — Rathna Kumar, co-writer

https://x.com/Filmyscoopss/status/2069279718613119418

Make no mistake about the scale of this. Allu Arjun is currently the most bankable face in the South, a star who can open a film in five languages at once. Lokesh is the rare director whose name on a poster is itself the marketing. Put them together and you get the kind of collaboration trade analysts whisper about for months — and this is Lokesh's **debut in Telugu cinema**, a crossing of the Vindhyas that carries its own freight of expectation.

The look test matters more than it sounds. In Lokesh's world, the look *is* the character. Think of Vikram's silver-stubbled stillness, Leo's coiled domesticity hiding a killer. An early teaser already showed Allu Arjun wearing the iconic silver *kada* that recurs across Lokesh's films, hinting at a stylish, Western-inspired tone. Reports say a couple of looks have already been zeroed in, and the final one will be locked in Mumbai before the cameras ever roll. When that face drops, the internet will lose a collective afternoon.

And the soundtrack of all this hype already exists. **Anirudh Ravichander** — the composer who has scored Lokesh's biggest swings — is attached for songs and background score, his first collaboration with Allu Arjun. The promotional "23 Theme" released during the initial announcement has already become an Instagram Reels staple, the kind of three-second sting that fans loop until it's muscle memory. Anirudh plus Allu Arjun plus Lokesh is, in the language of South cinema social media, a guaranteed "system hang."

The one piece still unlocked is the heroine. The casting rumour mill has been generous: **Pooja Hegde**, who sang *Monica* for Lokesh in *Coolie* and has worked with Allu Arjun twice before, is among the top contenders, while other reports float **Shraddha Kapoor** as a possible Bollywood import for the female lead. Either way, the leading lady will walk into one of the most scrutinised debuts-into-a-universe in recent memory.

So why the wait? Simple — Allu Arjun is a man with no free weekends. He is deep into **Raaka**, the heavily stylised action-thriller directed by **Atlee** and co-starring a pregnant **Deepika Padukone**, and he is squeezing the AA23 look test into a break from that shoot. Once *Raaka* wraps, he is expected to transition fully into Lokesh's universe. The film is bankrolled by **Mythri Movie Makers** (with BV Works), with principal photography expected to begin after Dasara and a pan-Indian release being eyed as early as December 2026, though the makers haven't formally committed to a date.

For the diaspora, this is the genre that travels best. Allu Arjun's *Pushpa* films were phenomena in the US and UK, packing midnight shows from New Jersey to Wembley, and Lokesh's *Leo* and *Vikram* drew the same overseas crowds who treat a Friday first-day-first-show like a festival. A pan-India actioner from these two, scored by Anirudh, releasing simultaneously in Hindi, Telugu, Tamil, Kannada and Malayalam, is precisely the kind of event that fills diaspora multiplexes and trends across three time zones at once.

For now, though, it all comes down to a chair, a mirror, and a director with very specific taste. Lock the look on June 25, and the floodgates open. The fans are already standing in the rain.
